flags.sentence: Keski-Uusimaa's crude 26.4% (95% CI 22.7–30.5) no-treatment-record share versus 27.5% nationally suggests relatively complete treatment recording, but county shares lack age and stage adjustment and pathway timestamps.
flags.problem: Overreach: the cited claim [cty:no_treatment_record:Keski_Uudenmaan_hyvinvointialue] states that 26.4% (95% CI 22.7–30.5) is not distinguishable from the national 27.5%, and [bs:coverage:Treatment_start] notes that the 27.5% share mixes untreated patients with unrecorded treatment; neither claim supports the conclusion that 26.4% versus 27.5% suggests relatively complete treatment recording.

flags.sentence: The crude share with no treatment record within 12 months is 26.4% (95% CI 22.7–30.5; n=127/481) versus 27.5% (4089/14873) nationally, with the 95% confidence interval including 27.5%; this mixes untreated patients and treatment that was not recorded, and as an inference, a data-quality signal below 27.5% is consistent with relatively complete treatment recording, not direct evidence.
flags.problem: Overreach: even framed as an inference, the cited claims do not support treating the county figure as a signal below 27.5% or consistent with relatively complete treatment recording, since [cty:no_treatment_record:Keski_Uudenmaan_hyvinvointialue] states it is not distinguishable from 27.5% and [bs:coverage:Treatment_start] notes that the 27.5% rate mixes untreated patients and unrecorded treatment.

flags.sentence: Public report data do not measure symptom onset or referrals, primary care visits are not included in the report's data and occupational health is not mentioned, imaging appears only indirectly as the diagnostic basis in approximately 20% of cases nationally, and specialist visits and treatments lack county waiting-time timestamps.
flags.problem: Minor imprecision in measure: [bs:coverage:Imaging] and [q:5eb155decc] state that approximately 20% is the share based on clinical examination alone, such as imaging, rather than imaging alone.

flags.sentence: Because the Health Care Act sets no legal maximum time for a cancer suspicion, the team recommends reporting access times using THL guidance Ohjaus 21/2016 definitions for 16 cancers and flagging stalled handovers, while the roadmap plans national target access times in 2026–2028 and the Filha programme's diagnostics guideline is due before the 2030 interim evaluation.
flags.problem: Plan presented with certainty: stating that the Filha programme's diagnostics guideline "is due" before the 2030 interim evaluation frames a future programme plan from [q:8f358a9de6] and [q:614febebf2] as a fixed deadline rather than something the programme plans or intends.
